body: A single `try` wraps the whole loop, so the first SendGrid failure (invalid or expired batch_id, rate limit, or hitting the same 100 pending-cancellation cap) exits the loop. None of the remaining reminders get cancelled. The `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls pushed so far are lazy PrismaPromises and never run either, because `Promise.all` is never reached. The failing reminder is picked up again on every cron run and blocks everything after it until its date passes, and all those emails go out. Put the try/catch inside each iteration and delete each reminder right after its cancel succeeds.

This deferred cancel misses emails due soon after the cancellation. The cron runs every 15 min, and the `deleteMany` above removes past-dated reminders before this query runs. Example: a booking is cancelled at 10:01 and its reminder is due at 10:10. The next run at 10:15 only sees a past-dated row and deletes it, but SendGrid already sent the email at 10:10. Anything that becomes `cancelled` less than one cron interval before its send time still gets delivered. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` should cancel right away at SendGrid when `scheduledDate` is within the cron window (for example within 1h), and only defer the rest.

The `immediateDelete` path does the same immediate POST /scheduled_sends cancel that this PR says hits SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit. It is still used for reschedules in handleNewBooking, which are frequent and high-volume, and for workflow/step deletion, where one workflow can have many reminders. Those callers will hit the cap again and emails will still go out. Also, this path never updates or deletes the DB row. After a reschedule, the old reminder stays with `scheduled: true` and is not marked `cancelled`, so the table disagrees with SendGrid.

Rescheduling still passes `immediateDelete = true`. The latest commit ("remove immediate delete for request reschedule") removed this flag in bookings.tsx, but it is still set here. Reschedules are the most common path, so they will fill SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation cap again, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix. Also, `try/catch` around a `forEach` of un-awaited async calls catches nothing. The helpers swallow their own errors, and any rejection would happen after this block has exited.

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are no longer awaited. Before, the DB deletes were collected and awaited in `Promise.all`. Now the `cancelled: true` update (or the delete) is fire-and-forget. On serverless (Vercel) the function can be frozen after the response is sent, before the update is written. The cron then never sees `cancelled` and the reminder email is still sent, which is the bug this PR is fixing. Collect these promises and await them. The same problem is in bookings.tsx (requestReschedule) and in workflows.tsx (activeOn removal and step edits).

The async `forEach` here calls the delete/cancel helpers without awaiting them. The code then schedules new reminders for the same bookings right away. If the request ends before the old rows are marked `cancelled`, both the old and new reminders get sent. Use `await Promise.all(remindersToUpdate.map(...))`.

Two problems when a workflow is deleted. First, each reminder triggers an immediate SendGrid cancel (`immediateDelete`), so a workflow with more than 100 scheduled emails hits the pending-cancellation cap again and the rest still go out. Second, these calls are not awaited, and `workflow.deleteMany` right below cascade-deletes the reminders, so `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`'s `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` races the cascade and can throw 'Record to delete does not exist' (it is swallowed). Await the cancellations before deleting the workflow. Using the deferred `cancelled` flag here doesn't work, because the rows are deleted by the cascade.
